source.citation: Hopewell S et al. CONSORT 2025 statement. BMJ 2025;389:e081123

items.1b: Structured summary of the trial design, methods, results, and conclusions
items.2: Name of trial registry, identifying number (with URL) and date of registration
items.3: Where the trial protocol and statistical analysis plan can be accessed
items.4: Where and how the individual de-identified participant data (including data dictionary), statistical code and any other materials can be accessed
items.5a: Sources of funding and other support (eg, supply of drugs), and role of funders in the design, conduct, analysis and reporting of the trial
items.5b: Financial and other conflicts of interest of the manuscript authors
items.7: Specific objectives related to benefits and harms
items.8: Details of patient or public involvement in the design, conduct and reporting of the trial
items.9: Description of trial design including type of trial (eg, parallel group, crossover), allocation ratio, and framework (eg, superiority, equivalence, non-inferiority, exploratory)
items.10: Important changes to the trial after it commenced including any outcomes or analyses that were not prespecified, with reason
items.11: Settings (eg, community, hospital) and locations (eg, countries, sites) where the trial was conducted
items.12b: If applicable, eligibility criteria for sites and for individuals delivering the interventions (eg, surgeons, physiotherapists)
items.13: Intervention and comparator with sufficient details to allow replication. If relevant, where additional materials describing the intervention and comparator (eg, intervention manual) can be accessed
items.14: Prespecified primary and secondary outcomes, including the specific measurement variable (eg, systolic blood pressure), analysis metric (eg, change from baseline, final value, time to event), method of aggregation (eg, median, proportion), and time point for each outcome
items.15: How harms were defined and assessed (eg, systematically, non-systematically)
items.16a: How sample size was determined, including all assumptions supporting the sample size calculation
items.16b: Explanation of any interim analyses and stopping guidelines
items.17a: Who generated the random allocation sequence and the method used
items.17b: Type of randomisation and details of any restriction (eg, stratification, blocking and block size)
items.18: Mechanism used to implement the random allocation sequence (eg, central computer/telephone; sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed containers), describing any steps to conceal the sequence until interventions were assigned
items.19: Whether the personnel who enrolled and those who assigned participants to the interventions had access to the random allocation sequence
items.20a: Who was blinded after assignment to interventions (eg, participants, care providers, outcome assessors, data analysts)
items.20b: If blinded, how blinding was achieved and description of the similarity of interventions
items.21a: Statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes, including harms
items.21b: Definition of who is included in each analysis (eg, all randomised participants), and in which group
items.21c: How missing data were handled in the analysis
items.21d: Methods for any additional analyses (eg, subgroup and sensitivity analyses), distinguishing prespecified from post hoc
items.22a: For each group, the numbers of participants who were randomly assigned, received intended intervention, and were analysed for the primary outcome
items.22b: For each group, losses and exclusions after randomisation, together with reasons
items.23a: Dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow-up for outcomes of benefits and harms
items.23b: If relevant, why the trial ended or was stopped
items.24a: Intervention and comparator as they were actually administered (eg, where appropriate, who delivered the intervention/comparator, how participants adhered, whether they were delivered as intended (fidelity))
items.24b: Concomitant care received during the trial for each group
items.25: A table showing baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group
items.26: For each primary and secondary outcome, by group:● the number of participants included in the analysis● the number of participants with available data at the outcome time point● result for each group, and the estimated effect size and its precision (such as 95% confidence interval)● for binary outcomes, presentation of both absolute and relative effect size
items.27: All harms or unintended events in each group
items.28: Any other analyses performed, including subgroup and sensitivity analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from post hoc
items.29: Interpretation consistent with results, balancing benefits and harms, and considering other relevant evidence
items.30: Trial limitations, addressing sources of potential bias, imprecision, generalisability, and, if relevant, multiplicity of analyses
